messages:
ravi: Quick spike writeup — want opinions on two patterns for private customer VPC connectivity to our control plane. TL;DR: lightweight in-VPC relay (single outbound mTLS stream) vs AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Pros/cons below, please react.

olivia: Nice, can you sketch auth/cert flow for the relay?

ravi: Sure — relay runs a tiny process in customer VPC (daemonset or single instance depending on Dedicated vs Private). It provisions a client cert via short-lived CSR to their KMS-backed onboarding token, then opens one long-lived mTLS connection to our control plane on 8443 and multiplexes control, metrics, logs. No inbound rules needed on customer side.

sam: Sounds good. Biggest win I see is NAT + TLS handshake reduction by reusing long connection. Also simpler for customers who can't accept inbound peering.

alex: But PrivateLink avoids us running anything inside customer account. Endpoint service gives an ENI in our VPC and the customer makes interface endpoint — no agents, more AWS-native.

maria: Tradeoff: PrivateLink charges per-hour + per-GB. For high telemetry volume that can add up versus single outbound connection through NAT. Also cross-account endpoint scale can hit ENI limits in high-tenant counts.

olivia: Security question: with relay we still need to limit what the relay can access in customer VPC. How do we prevent lateral movement?

ravi: Relay runs with a dedicated SG that only allows egress to our control plane FQNs and DNS. We recommend deploying it in a management subnet with restrictive IAM role with no SSM or instance profile permissions beyond cert CSR and metrics upload. Example SG: ```egress: - to: controlplane.corp.redwood-inference.internal:8443 protocol: tcp allow```.

sam: We should also gate relay creation via onboarding workflow so cert issuance needs a signed onboarding token tied to account id. If onboarding fails, relay service won't get a cert.

alex: PrivateLink simplifies that: we can bind VPC endpoint policies and require the customer to accept service permissions. No cert lifecycle in their account. But support surface for endpoint failures is bigger.

maria: Also consider inter-region: PrivateLink requires cross-region endpoints or inter-region traffic which can be awkward. Relay with outbound connection routes via nearest region egress and is simpler for low-latency control chatter.

olivia: Operationally, how do we do rollbacks or emergency isolation? If relay misbehaves, customer should be able to revoke cert or flip a security group. Need an emergency cutoff flow in console.

ravi: Agreed. Proposal: add a per-customer "control-plane enable" toggle in Console that triggers cert revocation and security-group update via Cloud API. Also provide a short RBAC runbook for SREs.

sam: For hosted customers with lots of tenants, I'd favour PrivateLink where customers already expect endpoint billing. For enterprise deals with regulatory constraints, relay is better because there's no provider-managed endpoint in customer VPC.

alex: What about HA? Relay should be a small ASG (2 instances across 2 AZs) or a K8s daemonset with anti-affinity. PrivateLink relies on AWS infra for HA.

maria: Cost model note: estimate per-customer monthly costs: PrivateLink ~ $40-$80 + data; relay minimal infra + NAT data charges. Need an experiment measuring telemetry bytes per customer to decide break-even.

ravi: Implementation checklist I'm proposing: 1) onboarding cert CSR flow + short-lived certs; 2) minimal relay binary + SG recommended template; 3) console toggle + cert revocation API; 4) PrivateLink offering for customers who request it; 5) cost telemetry experiment. Thoughts?

olivia: 👍 add a section for DNS/hostname verification — ensure mTLS validates the cert CN to account id.

sam: Also add metrics to track number of TLS connections we host and per-connection bytes so we can measure multiplexing wins.

maria: I'm +1 but insist we prototype in a single controlled customer first. Ops runbook and emergency cutover must be tested.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New branch pushed: feature/controlplane-relay-prototype -> staging. CI: 12/12 passed :rocket:

ravi: Great, I'll update the spike doc with these action items and schedule a short pairing session for the prototype next week. @maria @sam can you volunteer for on-call runbook test?

maria: I can do the runbook test.

sam: I can pair on metrics and prototype validation.

ravi: Thanks — will follow up with calendar invite. :thumbsup:
